name: comp-164

frames.best_why: The 4 CPU tile shows the lighter selected border, with the faded disabled tile still in view.

tagline: Core-count tiles in a grid; the chosen one brightens.
summary: A labelled grid of tile radios offering 2 to 16 CPU, three across and two deep, with the selected size outlined lighter. The 16 CPU tile is disabled and faded.
appearance: A small white heading sits above six rounded tiles with thin grey outlines on black, arranged in three columns and two rows. Each tile holds a centred white caption such as 2 CPU; the bottom-right one uses faded grey text.
behaviour: Clicking a tile swaps a lighter outline onto it. The recording opens with 2 CPU marked and moves to 4 CPU. The 16 CPU tile is disabled, so it never highlights or takes the selection.
demo_content: CPU Cores heading; 2 CPU, 4 CPU, 6 CPU, 8 CPU, 12 CPU, 16 CPU
search_phrases: pick how many cpu cores to use
grid of plan options with one disabled
choose a machine size in a grid
disabled option inside a tile group
use_when: When a machine or plan must be picked from a short list of fixed sizes on one screen.
avoid_when: One tile is hardcoded disabled, and the three-column grid grows tall once many sizes are listed.
customise: Sizes come from an items array inside the file; add, rename or disable entries there. Column count, gaps and the disabled fade are utility classes in the same file.
weight_why: Six plain tiles over a native radio group, with one short border fade.

a11y.note: Each tile is a label wrapping a hidden radio, so arrow keys select and a ring marks focus; the border fade ignores reduced-motion settings.

issues: The 16 CPU option is disabled for good, so the largest size can never be picked.
polish_why: Even grid with clear selected and disabled looks, but otherwise plain default styling.
